transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-11
Start: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Carlos Mejia (Redwood AE); Priya Raman (Redwood SE); Maya Chen (NovaPay - Head of MLOps); Ravi Patel (NovaPay - SRE); Elena Torres (NovaPay - PM)

Notes/Links shared: benchmark sheet: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/CRM-54721/latency.csv; internal perf doc: https://docs.redwood.com/poc/CRM-54721-kernel-profiling (redwood internal)

00:00 Carlos: ok thanks everyone for joining, quick checkin, this is our weekly POC sync for latency tuning, maya, ravi — you still see the same traffic shape?
00:12 Maya: yea, we're seeing the spike around 11am PST, mostly short queries, something like 40-50 tokens median but heavy tail to 1k sometimes, sorry i meant 800, uhm 800 tokens occasionally
00:26 Priya: that matches what we saw in the profiling — we pulled a sample trace from your staging and ran kernel-level microbenchmarks, i'll share the csv after, initial take: fused attention kernels improved TTFT by ~12% for median sequences
00:45 Ravi: when you say TTFT are we including network handshake and chunking cost for streaming? our main complaint is first token latency when we do user-facing completions
00:58 Priya: good question, so our TTFT here is from request receive to first token produced on the server-side, it excludes client-side network jitter; for streaming we measured both raw server TTFT and also end-to-end with a simulated client, raw server TTFT improved but end-to-end depends on chunk size
01:18 Elena: can you remind us the chunk sizes you tried? we tried 32 and 64 tokens before and saw weird variance
01:27 Priya: we tested chunk sizes of 8, 16, 32, 64. Smaller chunk sizes reduced time-to-first-token for short responses but increased per-token overhead. sweet spot for your workload (median 40-50) seems 16 or 32 with streaming enabled and KV cache warming enabled between calls
01:52 Carlos: ok, and kernel choices? you mentioned fused attention vs flash, what's the tradeoff there today?
02:02 Priya: fused attention gives better startup latency for smaller sequence lengths because it reduces kernel launch overhead; flash attention (or other mem-efficient kernels) helps throughput at long sequences but has slightly higher per-call startup in our tests on A100 and H100 variants. for NovaPay's tail we need to balance both — for short median we prefer fused for TTFT
02:30 Maya: our sequences flip a lot though — sometimes we get 800 token sage-like reports for support logs, you said you can route those to different model variant?
02:42 Priya: right, smart routing can route long sequences to a batch-optimized variant (quantized) with higher throughput and acceptable latency; short sequences hit a low-latency variant. we prototyped that in the POC and saw 8–15% cost savings while maintaining SLAs
03:00 Ravi: latency numbers, can you read the median and p95 from the sheet? the link is in the chat
03:07 Priya: reading from benchmark CSV: median TTFT (short path, fused kernels) ~42 ms; p95 ~210 ms; for streaming with chunk 16 median E2E TTFT ~65 ms; p95 ~260 ms. note these are server-side sim results, real network will add ~10–30 ms depending region
03:35 Elena: okay, p95 260 is acceptable for now but we want to get p95 under 200 if possible, what's realistic?
03:43 Priya: two levers — kernel-level (we're still testing an experimental fused/quantized path) which could shave another 10–12% on TTFT, and smart routing + cache warming to avoid cold KV cache for repeated users. combined might get you close to p95 ~180–190 in staging
04:05 Carlos: what about batch vs streaming? Rafael i mean Ravi's team is concerned about throughput cost too
04:12 Ravi: yes cost is a big one, we have to balance interactivity with per-token cost. if Streaming increases per-token overhead, cost goes up, right?
04:20 Priya: small chunk streaming does increase per-token overhead vs large batched decode, but because TTFT improves we converted many short tails to low-cost path; Redwood Optimize recommendations suggest dynamic chunk size by request type, and autoscaling can keep cost per token reasonable
04:40 Maya: security question — for Dedicated or Private, how do we handle KMS for model keys and logs? we need SOC2 and audit logs for compliance review
04:50 Carlos: yes for Dedicated/Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and we produce audit logs; we'll share SOC2/ISO docs in the follow-up. action: carlos to attach security bundle to the thread
05:02 Elena: earlier you mentioned KV cache warming; can you explain warm vs cold impact?
05:10 Priya: sure — cold KV cache on first token of a session forces recompute, warming avoids reloading the KV cache for frequently repeated prefixes. in our tests warming reduced median by ~8ms for sessions with repeated users, but it's workload dependent
05:32 Ravi: we can maybe prefetch for known returning users, we'll send a sample trace to show frequency of repeated prefixes
05:40 Maya: are there any model quantization tradeoffs that impact output quality? we saw some hallucination increase in a different POC after aggressive quantization
05:50 Priya: yes aggressive quantization (4-bit) can change numeric fidelity, tokenization artifacts for some prompts; Redwood's recommendation: use per-layer mixed quant profiles for long-form ticket generation and selective quant for short chat responses. we'll run a quality regression test on your prompt set after kernel changes
06:12 Carlos: on rollout—what's the canary plan if we flip to streaming fused kernels?
06:20 Priya: recommendation: 1) test in staging with your production trace; 2) canary 5% of traffic for 24–48 hours; 3) monitor TTFT, p95, error rates; 4) fallback to batch path automatically if regressions. we can automate the rollback rule in the console
06:40 Ravi: does the console expose token-level cost breakdown per route?
06:46 Carlos: yes, Redwood Console shows token-level cost, latency per route and model, and can alert on regressions. we'll share screenshots after this call
06:55 Maya: one more — for the long-seq tail, is it possible to offload to a cheaper quantized node pool and still maintain SLA?
07:03 Priya: absolutely, that's the routing policy we discussed — route >512 token requests to quantized batch pool, keep <512 on low-latency pool. can be region-aware too
07:18 Elena: ok sounds good. next steps recap?
07:22 Carlos: recap: Priya runs deeper kernel profiling with NovaPay's seq distribution and shares CSV by 8/14; Ravi provides production trace and seq histogram by 8/13; Carlos sends Dedicated pricing and security bundle by 8/16; schedule canary week of 8/18. any objections?
07:41 Maya: nope, sounds good
07:45 Ravi: fine
07:46 Carlos: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up in thread with links
07:50 (call ends)

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors present in names and acronyms; some timestamps approximate. The team referenced a shared benchmark CSV and an internal kernel profiling doc.
